verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              साङ्गा वेदा यथान्यायं येनाधीता महात्मना। यस्मिन्साक्षाद्धनुर्वेदो ह्रीनिषेवे प्रतिष्ठितः॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said Thai high-souled person who had duly studied the Vedas and their auxiliaries, he who had mastered this entire science of arms and who possessed modesty.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य प्रसादात्कुर्वन्ति कर्माणि पुरुषर्षभाः।  अमानुषाणि संग्रामे देवैरसुकराणि च॥२॥
verses.english: That Drona son of mighty sage, who had been insulted by the low-minded, cruel and mcan Dhristadyumna the slayer of his preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नाक्रुश्यति द्रोणे समक्षं पापकर्मणा।  नीचात्मना नृशंसेन क्षुद्रेण गुरुघातिना॥३॥
verses.english: That Drona through whose grace the foremost of men still achieve superhuman feats difficult of being achieved even by the gods and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit: नामर्षं तत्र कुर्वन्ति धिक्क्षात्रं धिगमर्षिताम्। पार्थाः सर्वे च राजानः पृथिव्यां ये धनुर्धराः॥४॥
verses.english: When that Drona suffered such an insult at the hands of that most sinful Dhristadyumna under the very eyes of all the warriors present, was there no Kshatriya who was then inspired with wrath? Fie on the Kshatriya order and fie on wrath itself!

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा किमाहुः पाञ्चाल्यं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              श्रुत्वा द्रुपदपुत्रस्य ता वाचः क्रूरकर्मणः॥५॥
verses.english: Tell me, O Sanjaya, what did the Parthas or the other kings of the earth, all illustrious warriors, say, having heard the words of the Panchala prince?

verses.sanskrit: तूष्णीं बभूवू राजानः सर्व एव विशांपते। अर्जुनस्तु कटाक्षेण जिह्मं विप्रेक्ष्य पार्षतम्॥६॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Hcaring those words of the ruthless son of Drupada, O king, all the rulers of the earth remained silent.

verses.sanskrit: स बाष्पमतिनिःश्वस्य धिग्धिगित्येव चाब्रवीत्। युधिष्ठिरश्च भीमश्च यमौ कृष्णस्तथाऽपरे॥७॥
verses.english: But Arjuna only casting side glances at Prisata's son and sighing and shedding copious tears said 'fie, fie.'

verses.sanskrit: आसन् सुव्रीडिता राजन् सात्यकिस्त्वब्रवीदिदम्। नेहास्ति पुरुषः कश्चिद्य इमं पापपूरुषम्॥८॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira and Bhima and the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) and Krishna himself were overwhelmed with shame, o king. Then Satyaki spoke these words-

verses.sanskrit: भाषमाणमकल्याणं शीघ्रं हन्यान्नराधमम्। एते त्वां पाण्डवाः सर्वे कुत्सयन्ति विवित्सया॥९॥
verses.english: Is there nobody that will quickly dispatch this sinful, low and cursed wretch, even when he is thus speaking?

verses.sanskrit: कर्मणा तेन पापेन श्वपाकं ब्राह्मणा इव।  एतत्कृत्वा महत्पापं निन्दितः सर्वसाधुभिः॥१०॥
verses.english: Like the Brahmanas blaming a Chandala, all these Pandavas are reproaching you for your having perpetrated his sinful act.

verses.sanskrit: न लज्जसे कथं वक्तुं समितिं प्राप्य शोभनाम्।  कथं च शतधा जिह्वा न ते मूर्धा च दीर्यते॥११॥
verses.english: Having perpetrated the most sinful act and condemned by the pious, do you not fell ashamed to open your lips in this august assemblage?

verses.sanskrit: गुरुमाक्रोशतः क्षुद्र न चाधर्मेण पात्यसे। वाच्यस्त्वमसि पार्थैश्च सर्वैश्चांधकवृष्णिभिः॥१२॥
verses.english: O despicable wretch, why did not your tongue and your cursed head go off into thousand fragments, when you were on the point of slaying your preceptor? Why were you not smitten down by that sinful act?

verses.sanskrit: यत्कर्म कलुषं कृत्वा श्लाघसे जनसंसदि।  अकार्यं तादृशं कृत्वा पुनरेव गुरुं क्षिपन्॥१३॥
verses.english: You richly merit the condemnation of the Parthas and all the Vrishnis and the Andhakas inasmuch as perpetrating this sinful act, you are boasting of it in the presence of this august assembly.

verses.sanskrit: वध्यस्त्वं न त्वयार्थोऽस्ति मुहूर्तमपि जीवता।  कस्त्वेतद्व्यवसेदार्यस्त्वदन्यः पुरुषाधम॥१४॥
verses.english: Having committed the most heinous act of sin, you further reveal you hatred for the preceptor. For this you deserve to be slain; there is no use in sparing your life even for a moment.

verses.sanskrit: निगृह्य केशेषु वधं गुरोर्धर्मात्मनः सतः।  सप्तावरे तथा पूर्वे बान्धवास्ते निमज्जिताः॥१५॥
verses.english: What other sinful wretch, except yourself, will dare cause the virtuous preceptor's death, holding him by his hoary locks?

verses.sanskrit: यशसा च परित्यक्तास्त्वां प्राप्य कुलपांसनम्। उक्तवांश्चापि यत्पार्थे भीष्मं प्रति नरर्षभ॥१६॥
verses.english: Having obtained you-the disgrace to their race-for their descendant, seven generations before you and seven after, in your race, have sunk in hell, being deprived of their glory.

verses.sanskrit: तथाऽन्तो विहितस्तेन स्वयमेव महात्मना।  तस्यापि तव सोदर्यो निहन्ता पापकृत्तमः॥१७॥
verses.english: You have accused Partha that foremost of men with the slaughter of Bhisma. But this latter illustrious personage has hiinself caused his own destruction.

verses.sanskrit: नान्यः पाञ्चाल्यपुत्रेभ्यो विद्यते भुवि पापकृत्। स चापि सृष्टः पित्रा ते भीष्मस्यांतकरः किल॥१८॥
verses.english: Indeed that vilest of wretches viz., your uterine brother Sikhandin, was the cause of Bhisma's death. Really there is no one more sinful on the face of the earth, than the sons of Panchala king

verses.sanskrit: शिखण्डी रक्षितस्तेन स च मृत्युर्महात्मनः। पञ्चालाश्चलिता धर्मात्क्षुद्रा मित्र-गुरुद्रुहः॥१९॥
verses.english: Your father had begotten Sikhandin for the slaughter of Bhishma. As regards Arjuna he only protected your brother when he caused the death of the high-souled Bhishma.

verses.sanskrit: त्वां प्राप्य सहसोदर्यं धिक्कृतं सर्वसाधुभिः। पुनश्चेदीदृशीं वाचं मत्समीपे वदिष्यसि॥२०॥
verses.english: The Panchalas have gone astray from the paths of rectitude and like despicable wretches they are injuring their friends and their preceptors, only for having obtained yourself and your brother, hated by the pious, among themselves.

verses.sanskrit: शिरस्ते पोथयिष्यामि गदया वज्रकल्पया। त्वां च ब्रह्महणं दृष्ट्वा जनः सूर्यमवेक्षते॥२१॥
verses.english: If you again speak such words before re, I shall knock down your head with a mace resembling the bolt of heaven.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्महत्या हि ते पापं प्रायश्चित्तार्थमात्मनः। पाञ्चालक सुदुर्वृत्त ममैव गुरुमग्रतः॥२२॥
verses.english: Stained as you are with the sin of Brahmanicide, people looking at you the slayer of a Brahmana, have to look at the Sun for purifying themselves.

verses.sanskrit: गुरोर्गुरुं च भूयोऽपि क्षिपन्नैव हि लज्जसे। तिष्ठ तिष्ठ सहस्वैकं गदापातमिमं मम॥२३॥
verses.english: Ill-mannered wretch of Panchala, villifying my own preceptor in the first instance and then my preceptor's preceptor, why don't you feel ashamed?

verses.sanskrit: तव चापि सहिष्येऽहं गदापाताननेकशः। सात्त्वतेनैवमाक्षिप्तः पार्षतः परुषाक्षरम्॥२४॥
verses.english: 'Wait, Wait.' Bear but this single stroke of my mace. I will bear many strokes of that of yours."

verses.sanskrit:
संरब्धं सात्यकिं प्राह संक्रुद्धः प्रहसन्निव।
              धृष्टद्युम्न उवाच।
              श्रूयते श्रूयते चेति क्षम्यते चेति माधव॥२५॥
verses.english: Thus reproached by that scion of the Satvata race, Prisata's son inspired with wrath, addressed these harsh words to the enraged Satyaki.

verses.sanskrit: सदाऽनार्योऽशुभः साधुं पुरुषं क्षेप्तुमिच्छति। क्षमा प्रशस्यते लोके न तु पापोऽर्हति क्षमाम्॥२६॥
verses.english: Dhristadyumna said O you of Madhu's race, I have heard you speak. But I forgive you; yourself sinful and impious, you desire to throw odium on the righteous?

verses.sanskrit: क्षमावन्तं हि पापात्मा जितोऽयमिति मन्यते। स त्वं क्षुद्रसमाचारो नीचात्मा पापनिश्चयः॥२७॥
verses.english: Forgiveness is a praise worthy virtue, buy sinful wretches do not deserve it. A wicked fellow regards him who shows forgiveness as powerless (lit : conquered).

verses.sanskrit: आकेशाग्रान्नखाग्राच्च वक्तव्यो वक्तुमिच्छसि। यः स भूरिश्रवाश्छिन्नभुजः प्रायगतस्त्वया॥२८॥
verses.english: Ill-behaved, of low mind and sinful resolutions, you are condemnable from the end of your hair to the tip of your toe. Yet do you desire to censure others?

verses.sanskrit: वार्यमाणेन हि हतस्ततः पापतरं नु किम्। गाहमानो मया द्रोणो दिव्येनास्त्रेण संयुगे॥२९॥
verses.english: What act can be more unrighteous than that perpetrated by you when, repeatedly prevented, you slew Bhurisrava, whose arm was lopped off and who had betaken to the Praya Yoga?

verses.sanskrit: विसृष्टशस्त्रो निहतः किं तत्र क्रूर दुष्कृतम्। अयुध्यमानं यस्त्वाजौ तथा प्रायगतं मुनिम्॥३०॥
verses.english: Arranging his troops in order Drona was fighting with his celestial weapons he laid aside his weapons and I slew him o crooked one, what is there improper in this?

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नबाहुं परैर्हन्यात्सात्यके स कथं वदेत्। निहत्य त्वां पदा भूमौ स विकर्षति वीर्यवान्॥३१॥
verses.english: How can he, O Satyaki, censure such as act, who himself has slain his opponent, desisted from battle an opponent that was sitting in Praya Yoga and whose arm was cut-off by another.

verses.sanskrit: किं तदा न निहंस्येनं भूत्वा पुरुषसत्तमः। त्वया पुनरनार्येण पूर्वं पार्थेन निर्जितः॥३२॥
verses.english: That puissant opponent of yours, careered on the field having thrown you down with the stroke of his feet. Foremost if you were of all male beings why did you not then slay him?

verses.sanskrit: यदा तदा हतः शूरः सौमदत्तिः प्रतापवान्। यत्र यत्र तु पाण्डूनां द्रोणो द्रावयते चमूम्॥३३॥
verses.english: When Partha had already vanquished him, it was only then that by an unfair means you slew the puissant son of Somadatta.

verses.sanskrit: किरञ्छरसहस्राणि तत्र तत्र प्रयाम्यहम्। स त्वमेवंविधं कृत्वा कर्मचाण्डालवत्स्वयम्॥३४॥
verses.english: In whatever quarter Drona had sought to rout the troops of the Pandavas, in that quarter I proceeded, shooting myriads of shafts.

verses.sanskrit: वक्तुमर्हसि वक्तव्यः कस्मात्त्वं परुषाण्यथ। कर्ता त्वं कर्मणो ह्यस्य नाहं वृष्णिकुलाधम॥३५॥
verses.english: Having yourself perpetrated an act worthy of a Chandala only, it is strange that you desire to censure me in such a vile language.

verses.sanskrit: पापानां च त्वमावासः कर्मणां मा पुनर्वद। जोषमास्व न मां भूयो वक्तुमर्हस्यतः परम्॥३६॥
verses.english: You are the perpetrator of vile acts and not I, O vilest of the Vrishni race. You are the hotbed of sin. Do not again blame this deed of mine.

verses.sanskrit: अधरोत्तरमेतद्धि यन्मां त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि। अथ वक्ष्यसि मां मौर्ख्याद्भूयः परुषमीदृशम्॥३७॥
verses.english: Hold your tongue. It is improper that you shall move after this. I give you this reply from my own lips, you should not address me any longer.

verses.sanskrit: गमयिष्यामि बाणैस्त्वां युधि वैवस्वतक्षयम्। न चैवं मूर्ख धर्मेण केवलेनैव शक्यते॥३८॥
verses.english: If again, out of folly you speak such harsh words to me, I shall dispatch you to the abode of Death with my own arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामपि ह्यधर्मेण चेष्टितं शृणु यादृशम्। वञ्चितः पाण्डवः पूर्वमधर्मेण युधिष्ठिरः॥३९॥
verses.english: Once cannot overcome his foes, O fool, solely through fair means. Hear how our opponents also acted unfairly.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदी च परिक्लिष्टा तथाऽधर्मेण सात्यके। प्रव्राजिता वनं सर्वे पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया॥४०॥
सर्वस्वमपकृष्टं च तथाऽधर्मेण बालिश। अधर्मेणापकृष्टश्च मद्रराजः परेरितः॥४१॥
verses.english: The Pandavas with Krishna their wife were also exiled to the woods and fool, all their possessions were robbed out of them by unrighteous means.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्मेण तथा बालः सौभद्रो विनिपातितः। इतोऽप्यधर्मेण हतो भीष्मः परपुरञ्जयः॥४२॥
verses.english: The king of the Madras was again weaned away from our side by an act of unrighteousness by the foe, unfairly also was the tender son of Subhadra slain.

verses.sanskrit: भूरिश्रवा ह्यधर्मेण त्वया धर्मविदा हतः। एवं परैराचरितं पाण्डवेयैश्च संयुगे॥४३॥
verses.english: Now for the Pandavas, the grand-father of the Kurus, Bhishma was slain by an act of unrighteousness. Bhurisrava was unfairly slain by your very justicel-oving self.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षमाणैर्जयं वीरैर्धर्मज्ञैरपि सात्वत। दुर्ज्ञेयः स परो धर्मस्तथाऽधर्मश्च दुर्विदः॥४४॥
verses.english: Thus, O you of the Salvata race, the heroic Pandavas and the Kurus have both acted sinfully for victory in battle, although they are all conversant with the rules of morality.

verses.sanskrit:
युध्यस्व कौरवैः सार्धं मा गाः पितृनिवेशनम्।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवमादीनि वाक्यानि क्रूराणि परुषाणि च॥४५॥
verses.english: Thus morality is a mystery, as also immorality is difficult of being ascertained. Fight on with the Kauravas and do not return to the home of your fathers.

verses.sanskrit: श्रावितः सात्यकिः श्रीमानाकम्पित इवाभवत्। तच्छ्रुत्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षः सात्यकिस्त्वाददे गदाम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Addressed in such ruthless and harsh words, the handsome Satyaki trembled from hcad to foot.

verses.sanskrit: विनिःश्वस्य यथा सर्पः प्रणिधाय रथे धनुः। ततोऽभिपत्य पाञ्चाल्यं संरंभेणेदमब्रवीत्॥४७॥
verses.english: Hearing those words Satyaki with his eyes coppery in rage, laid his bow aside on the car and breathing like a snake he grasped his mace.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वां वक्ष्यामि परुषं हनिष्ये त्वां वधक्षमम्। तमापतन्तं सहसा महाबलममर्षणम्॥४८॥
verses.english: Then advancing furiously upon the Panchala prince he said-"I shall not waste my harsh words on you any longer, but I shall crush you, as you richly deserve to be slaughtered."

verses.sanskrit: पाञ्चाल्यायाभिसंक्रुद्धमन्तकायान्तकोपमम्। चोदितो वासुदेवेन भीमसेनो महाबलः॥४९॥
verses.english: Beholding the puissant Satyaki rush, from wrath and desire for revenge, at the Panchala prince, like Death against a match of his.

verses.sanskrit: अवप्लुत्य रथात्तूर्णं बाहुभ्यां समवारयत्। द्रवमाणं तथा क्रुद्धं सात्यकिं पाण्डवो बली॥५०॥
verses.english: The mighty Bhima urged by Vasudeva, quickly jumped down from his chariot and caught hold of him by the arms.

verses.sanskrit: प्रस्पन्द‌मानमादाय जगाम बलिनं बलात्। स्थित्वा विष्टभ्य चरणौ भीमेन शिनिपुङ्गवः॥५१॥
verses.english: The puissant Satyaki, who was then furiously rushing (at Dhristadyumna) advanced a few steps, dragging after him the mighty son of Pandu, who was trying to withhold him.

verses.sanskrit: निगृहीतः पदे षष्ठे बलेन बलिनां वरः। अवरुह्य रथात्तूर्णं ध्रियमाणं बलीयसा॥५२॥
verses.english: Then Bhima firmly planting his feet, succeeded in stopping that foremost of all beings endowed with strength viz., that illustrious scion or Shini's race.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा सहदेवो विशांपते। अस्माकं पुरुषव्याघ्र मित्रमन्यन्न विद्यते॥५३॥
verses.english: Then, Oking, Sahadeva jumping down from his car, addressed Satyaki held in check by the strong arms of Bhima, in these soothing

verses.sanskrit: परमन्धकवृष्णिभ्यः पञ्चालेभ्यश्च मारिष। तथैवान्धकवृष्णीनां तथैव च विशेषतः॥५४॥
verses.english: O foremost of men, we possess not friends dearer to ourselves, then the Andhakas, the Vrishnis and the Panchalas, O descendant of Madhu's race.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णस्य च तथाऽस्मत्तो मित्रमन्यन्न विद्यते। पञ्चालानां च वार्ष्णेय समुद्रान्तां विचिन्वताम्॥५५॥
verses.english: Similarly the Andhakas and the Vrishnis, specially Krishna among the latter, cannot have any friend dearer than ourselves.

verses.sanskrit: नान्यदस्ति परं मित्रं यथा पाण्डववृष्णयः। स भवानीदृशं मित्रं मन्यते च यथा भवान्॥५६॥
verses.english: The Panchalas also, O scion of the Vrishni race, will not be able to find friends dearer to themselves than the Vrishnis and the Pandavas, even if they search the whole earth to the very boundaries of the seas.

verses.sanskrit: भवन्तश्च यथाऽस्माकं भवतां च तथा वयम्। स एवं सर्वधर्मज्ञ मित्रधर्ममनुस्मरन्॥५७॥
verses.english: You are a dear friend to this prince and even such is he to you. You are to us even as we are to you.

verses.sanskrit: नियच्छ मन्युं पाञ्चाल्यात् प्रशाम्य शिनिपुङ्गव। पार्षतस्य क्षम त्वं वै क्षमतां पार्षतश्च ते॥५८॥
verses.english: Versed in the rules of duty, restrain your anger having the prince of the Panchalas for its object, remembering the duties that you owe to you friends.

verses.sanskrit: वयं क्षमयितारश्च किमन्यत्र शमाद्भवेत्। प्रशाम्यमाने शैनेये सहदेवेन मारिष॥५९॥
verses.english: Forgive the son of Prisata, let him also forgive you. We will also practise forgiveness. What other virtue can be equal to forgiveness!

verses.sanskrit: पाञ्चालराजस्य सुतः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्। मुञ्च मुञ्च शिनेः पौत्रं भीम युद्धमदान्वितम्॥६०॥
verses.english: When, O sire, Sahadeva was thus pacifying the grandson of Shini, the son of the Panchala king thus smilingly spoke:मुञ्चमुञ्च शिनेः पौत्रं भीम युद्धमदान्वितम्॥

verses.sanskrit: आसादयतु मामेष धराधरमिवानिलः। यावदस्य शितैर्बाणैः संरंभं विनयाम्यहम्॥६१॥
verses.english: Bhima, let the grandson of Shini, so proud of his prowess in battle, he released. Let him encounter me like the wind encountering the mountains.

verses.sanskrit: युद्धश्रद्धां च कौन्तेय जीवितं चास्य संयुगे। किं नु शक्यं मया कर्तुं कार्यं यदिदमुद्यतम्॥६२॥
verses.english: I shall smother his wrath with my sharp arrows, as also his itching for battle; O son of Kunti, let me deprive him of his life in battle.

verses.sanskrit: सुमहत्पाण्डुपुत्राणामायान्त्येते हि कौरवाः। अथवा फाल्गुनः सर्वान्वारयिष्यति संयुगे॥६३॥
verses.english: I am alone competent to achieve the mighty task the sons of Pandu have undertaken, heavy though it may be. Yonder come the Kauravas.

verses.sanskrit: अहमप्यस्य मूर्धानं पातयिष्यामि सायकैः। मन्यते च्छिन्नबाहुं मां भूरिश्रवसमाहवे॥६४॥
verses.english: Or Phalguna himself will hold all of them in check. Let me cut-off this one's head with my arrows.

verses.sanskrit: उत्सृजैनमहं चैनमेष वा मां हनिष्यति। शृण्वन्पाञ्चालवाक्यानि सात्यकिः सर्पवच्छ्वसन्॥६५॥
verses.english: He takes me for Bhurisravas with his arm lopped off. Leave him, Either I will slay him or he shall slay me

verses.sanskrit: भीमबाह्वन्तरे सक्तो विस्फुरत्यनिशं बली। तौ वृषाविव नर्दन्तौ बलिनौ बाहुशालिनौ॥६६॥
त्वरया वासुदेवश्च धर्मराजश्च मारिष। यत्नेन महता वीरौ वारयामासतुस्ततः॥६७॥
निवार्य परमेष्वासौ कोपसंरक्तलोचनौ। युयुत्सूनपरान्संख्ये प्रतीयुः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥६८॥
verses.english: With great difficulty restrained those two heroes. Thus restraining those two mighty bowmen, whose eyes were red in rage, the foremost of the Kshatriyas advanced desirous of meeting the foe in battle.
